title: Agentry agent.yaml manifest (schema major 2)
description: Machine form of the QuickAgent manifest: a release declares the run modes it supports (autonomous, interactive) and one instruction entrypoint. Closed schema: unknown keys are invalid everywhere (rule V1). This schema covers the static shape; the context rules V2 (repo identity), V3 (tag equality and channel monotonicity), V4 (include resolution, instruction file present), V7 (public-publish LICENSE/README and SPDX allowlist), V8 (archive quotas) and V9 (frontmatter vs manifest) are enforced by the registry and by pkg/manifest, as are glob validity and the policy-gated "*" egress.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest schema major; this file describes major "2".

name.description: Agent name; must match the target repo (V2) and the registry's handle pattern.

namespace.description: Namespace handle; must match the target repo (V2) and the registry's handle pattern.

modes.description: Run modes the release supports; one or both (V1).

version.description: Strict semver without a leading v; must equal the git tag and exceed every existing version on its channel (V3).

summary.description: Plain single-line text, at most 140 characters (V8).

license.description: SPDX license id; required and checked against the embedded allowlist for public publish (V7).

instruction.description: Repo-relative instruction file; AGENT.md when omitted. A leading YAML frontmatter block is stripped by consumers, so a SKILL.md-shaped file works unchanged. Must exist and be matched by publish.include (V4).

intake.description: Questions asked before a run starts, in either mode (V10). The runner stages the answers read-only for the agent; secret answers are injected as run-scoped secrets, never as text.

interactive.description: Hints for interactive sessions (V10). Limits here can only tighten runner policy.

opening.description: The assistant's first message when no task text was given. It may span lines; it carries no other control character and no format character (V10).

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: End the session after this much silence; policy caps it.

guide.description: The author's words for the run setup, shown to people before a run and never to the agent (V10). Clients derive the same steps from the rest of the manifest when it is absent.

overview.description: What the QuickAgent does and returns, in markdown. At most 4096 bytes (V10 counts bytes). Newlines and tabs are the only control characters it may carry.

prepare.description: What to gather before starting, one plain line each.

files.description: What files to bring to the run, in one plain line.

task.description: The placeholder for the task field.

connect.description: Help per declared secret name: where to create the key and which scopes it needs, in markdown a person reads (never the agent). At most 2,000 characters each; newlines and tabs are the only control characters it may carry. Every key must be a secret the release declares, in capabilities.secrets or a declared MCP server's secrets (V10; JSON schema cannot express that cross-reference).

knowledge.description: The knowledge packs the release ships in its archive under knowledge/<name>/, and what a person may attach of their own (V11). Each shipped pack is the CLI's layout (manifest.json, wiki/ with index.md and log.md, sources/), at most 10 MB and 2,000 files, outside the archive's own quotas (V8), and scanned with the version. A newly shipped name widens the contract; accepts is shown to people only.

name.description: The pack's name and its directory under knowledge/.

prompt.description: One plain line shown in the run setup's Knowledge step, never to the agent.

required.description: The Knowledge step cannot be skipped.

inputs.description: What files the QuickAgent takes and which view of them its agent reads by default (V12). Absent, any kind is taken and each file keeps its own default view: the text a decoder made where one made it, anything else as uploaded. It grants nothing: attaching a file is the grant, so the block is outside the contract.

kinds.description: The kinds of file it takes, for the run setup and the Drafter: documents (PDFs, office documents, e-books), code (source, markup, configuration, a repository), data (CSV, JSON, YAML, spreadsheets, logs), images (photographs, scans, screenshots, diagrams), or any, which is declared alone. Absent means any.

view.description: The view the agent reads an input in by default: text (the text a decoder made: a document's, an image's, HTML's Markdown; the upload for a file with none), original (the file as uploaded), or both (each file's own default, with both views offered). Absent means both, and both is read exactly as absent. The default never removes a view an input has.

interfaces.description: Export formats for `agentry install --target`; unrelated to mode.

capabilities.description: THE security contract; closed vocabulary (V5). Empty = pure text. Identical in both modes: an interactive session cannot widen it.

secrets.description: Environment variable NAMES the agent expects; never values.

optionalSecrets.description: The declared secrets (the agent's own or a declared MCP server's) a run can do without; every other declared secret is required. Each must be declared (V5); names only, never values.

targetHosts.description: The intake questions of type host (V14): each is a target host, a machine the person names when the run starts, that the agent may run commands on and administer through the runner's host tools. Names only; the release never names the host, its address, user or port.

browser.description: A headless web browser for the run (V15): the sites the person names when the run starts (url questions), the fixed hosts its pages need, its scope, and the declared secrets it may type into the site's forms. Site scope (the default) admits the sites, their subdomains and the hosts; public admits any public site and is treated as "*" egress by publication policy. A browser that types secrets cannot have public scope.

sites.description: Ids of intake questions of type url: the person's answer to each is a site the browser may open, with its subdomains.

hosts.description: Fixed hosts the browser may also reach: an exact DNS name or a *. suffix. No address, no port.

secrets.description: Declared secrets (in capabilities.secrets or optionalSecrets) the browser may type by name; the value never reaches the model.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the agent uses to do its job.

include.description: Archive ALLOWLIST of glob patterns; segments use path.Match syntax and a whole "**" segment matches any number of segments (V4).

relPath.description: Repo-root-relative slash-separated path: not absolute, no "." or ".." segments, no empty segments, no backslashes.

includePattern.description: Like relPath but glob syntax: path.Match per segment plus whole-segment "**"; backslash escapes allowed. Bracket-class validity is checked by pkg/manifest.

hostName.description: Exact DNS host name: dot-separated labels of 1-63 alphanumeric-or-hyphen characters, no leading/trailing hyphen.

egressHost.description: One egress list element: an exact DNS host or "*" (policy-gated). "none" is only valid as the entire egress value.

egress.description: "none", "*" (policy-gated), or a list of exact DNS hosts.

mcpServer.description: A declared MCP server: a package (npm or pypi, with an exact version) or a remote server (url, with auth). Exactly one of npm, pypi or url; pkg/manifest holds the cross-field rules this schema cannot express.

url.description: A remote server's HTTPS address: a public lowercase host name, port 443, no user information, query or fragment. pkg/manifest refuses IP literals and internal names.

auth.description: How a remote server is signed in to: oauth (the person's connection), secret (its one declared secret as a bearer header) or none.

version.description: Exact version to install (a package server only).

env.description: Plain, non-secret configuration the server reads from its environment. A name that is also a declared secret is refused by pkg/manifest. Values are literal: one the runner's gateway would rewrite — a `$` followed by a name character, `{` or a special shell parameter, or a `{{…}}` template — is refused.

mcpOAuth.description: A package server's OAuth sign-in: the runner makes or reuses the person's connection with the issuer and renders the access token, and only the access token, into files and env. {access_token} must appear in a template or an env value (pkg/manifest).

path.description: A plain file name in the token folder.

template.description: The file's content. Placeholders: {access_token}, {expiry} (RFC 3339 UTC), {expiry_ms} (Unix milliseconds).

additionalProperties.description: Placeholders: {access_token}, and {dir}, the token folder's path.

id.description: Answer key; unique within the manifest.

prompt.description: One plain line: no control character and no format character (V10).

type.description: The answer's shape. host asks for a target host, [user@]host[:port], that the runner reaches over SSH; its id is listed in capabilities.targetHosts (V14). repository and url ask for an input source (V13): fetched before the run into /inputs/<id>/, with an optional access token asked for by the run setup. A source question grants nothing and needs no capabilities entry.

version.description: Semver constraint (e.g. "^1.2"); absent means any. Constraint syntax is validated by pkg/manifest.
